name: Occipitofrontalis
function: Two-bellied scalp muscle joined by the galea aponeurotica; the frontal belly raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead, the occipital belly retracts the scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Frontal belly: galea aponeurotica. Occipital belly: lateral two-thirds of superior nuchal line and mastoid part of temporal bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Frontal belly: skin of eyebrows and root of nose (blends with orbicularis oculi/procerus). Occipital belly: galea aponeurotica

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Frontal belly: temporal branches of CN VII. Occipital belly: posterior auricular branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates eyebrows, wrinkles forehead (surprise); occipitalis retracts scalp

pearl: Forehead sparing separates an upper motor neuron (stroke) facial palsy from Bell palsy: the frontalis region of the facial nucleus receives bilateral cortical input.

name: Orbicularis oculi
function: Sphincter of the eyelids: the palpebral part blinks gently, the orbital part squeezes the eyes shut, and the lacrimal part pumps tears into the lacrimal sac.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Nasal part of frontal bone, frontal process of maxilla, medial palpebral ligament, lacrimal bone (orbital, palpebral and lacrimal parts)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin around the orbit, lateral palpebral raphe, tarsal plates

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal and zygomatic branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Closes eyelids (palpebral part: blink; orbital part: forceful closure); aids lacrimal drainage

pearl: CN VII palsy causes lagophthalmos (incomplete eye closure) with exposure keratitis; test by squeezing eyes shut against resistance. Bell phenomenon (protective upward globe roll) is seen through the open lid.

name: Corrugator supercilii
function: Draws the eyebrow medially and downward, producing the vertical glabellar frown lines.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial end of the superciliary arch of the frontal bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the middle of the eyebrow

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Pulls eyebrow medially and inferiorly (frowning, squinting in bright light)

pearl: Prime target of botulinum toxin for glabellar frown lines; the toxin cleaves SNAP-25 and blocks acetylcholine release for about 3 months.

name: Procerus
function: Pulls the medial eyebrow down and wrinkles the skin over the root of the nose (horizontal radix line across the nasal bridge). Oblique 'bunny lines' on the nasal sidewalls are from nasalis, not procerus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Fascia over the nasal bone and upper lateral nasal cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the glabella between the eyebrows

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal (and zygomatic) branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses medial end of eyebrow; produces transverse wrinkles over the root of the nose

pearl: Treated together with corrugator in cosmetic botulinum toxin injections; a fixed procerus contraction (the 'procerus sign') gives the worried stare of progressive supranuclear palsy.

name: Nasalis
function: Transverse part compresses the nostril, alar part flares the nostril; the main muscle of the external nose.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Maxilla above and lateral to the incisive fossa (transverse part) and over the lateral incisor (alar part)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Aponeurosis across the nasal dorsum (transverse part); skin and alar cartilage of the nostril (alar part)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Compressor naris narrows the nostril; dilator naris flares it

pearl: Nasal flaring from the alar part is a sign of increased work of breathing, especially in infants with bronchiolitis or pneumonia.

name: Levator labii superioris
function: Elevates the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold (sneering, exposing the maxillary teeth).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Infraorbital margin of the maxilla, above the infraorbital foramen

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin and muscle of the upper lip

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the upper lip; deepens the nasolabial furrow

pearl: The infraorbital nerve (V2) emerges deep to it at the infraorbital foramen; an infraorbital nerve block here anesthetizes the upper lip, lower eyelid and lateral nose.

name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
function: Flares the nostril and elevates the medial part of the upper lip, deepening the upper nasolabial fold (snarl).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Frontal process of the maxilla

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Alar cartilage and skin of the nose (medial slip) and skin of the upper lip (lateral slip)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Zygomatic and buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Flares the nostril and raises the upper lip medially

pearl: Hyperactivity lifts the lip excessively (the 'gummy smile' or Elvis snarl); low-dose botulinum toxin near its origin lowers the lip. Like all facial expression muscles it is a 2nd pharyngeal arch derivative supplied by CN VII.

name: Zygomaticus major
function: Draws the angle of the mouth upward and laterally; the principal smiling muscle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic bone, anterior to the zygomaticotemporal suture

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Zygomatic and buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and retracts the angle of the mouth (smiling, laughing)

pearl: Smile asymmetry is the bedside test of lower facial weakness; an upper motor neuron lesion drops the contralateral smile but spares the forehead.

name: Zygomaticus minor
function: Elevates the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial furrow, exposing the maxillary teeth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic bone, just behind the zygomaticomaxillary suture (anteromedial to zygomaticus major)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper lip, lateral to levator labii superioris

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the upper lip; contributes to the nasolabial fold

pearl: Blunting or flattening of the nasolabial fold on one side is an early sign of facial weakness in stroke or Bell palsy.

name: Levator anguli oris
function: Raises the angle of the mouth and deepens the nasolabial furrow; lies deep to the zygomatic muscles and levator labii superioris.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Canine fossa of the maxilla, just below the infraorbital foramen

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates the angle of the mouth (smiling)

pearl: The infraorbital nerve and vessels run between levator anguli oris and levator labii superioris, the plane entered during an infraorbital nerve block.

name: Risorius
function: Retracts the angle of the mouth laterally, producing a grin or grimace.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Fascia over the parotid gland and masseter

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Modiolus and skin at the angle of the mouth

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Draws the corner of the mouth laterally (grinning)

pearl: Risus sardonicus of tetanus (or strychnine poisoning) is sustained spasm of risorius and other facial muscles; the muscle is variable and absent in some people.

name: Buccinator
function: Compresses the cheek against the teeth to keep food on the occlusal surface during chewing, and drives air out of the mouth when blowing or sucking.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible opposite the molars; pterygomandibular raphe

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Modiolus and orbicularis oris at the angle of the mouth

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal branches of CN VII (motor); buccal nerve of V3 is sensory to the overlying mucosa

details.label: Action
details.value: Presses cheek against teeth; expels air (trumpeter's muscle); assists sucking

pearl: Pierced by the parotid (Stensen) duct opposite the 2nd maxillary molar; in CN VII palsy food pools in the vestibule. Cheek sensation is V3 (buccal nerve), motor is VII.

name: Orbicularis oris
function: Sphincter of the mouth: closes, purses and protrudes the lips; essential for speech, whistling, sucking and keeping food in the mouth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Modiolus and fibers of buccinator and other perioral muscles; maxilla and mandible near the midline

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Buccal and marginal mandibular branches of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Closes and protrudes the lips (kissing, whistling); shapes lips for speech

pearl: Inability to whistle, puff out the cheeks or hold air in the mouth indicates lower facial weakness (CN VII palsy, myasthenia gravis, facioscapulohumeral dystrophy).

name: Depressor anguli oris
function: Pulls the angle of the mouth downward and laterally (frowning, expressing sadness).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Oblique line of the mandible below the canine and premolar teeth

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Modiolus and skin at the angle of the mouth

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Marginal mandibular branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses the angle of the mouth (frowning)

pearl: The marginal mandibular branch of CN VII runs along the lower border of the mandible deep to platysma; injury during submandibular or neck surgery causes an asymmetric frown.

name: Depressor labii inferioris
function: Draws the lower lip downward and laterally and everts it (pouting, showing the lower teeth).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Oblique line of the mandible between the symphysis and the mental foramen

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the lower lip, blending with orbicularis oris

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Marginal mandibular branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses and everts the lower lip

pearl: Marginal mandibular nerve injury (submandibular surgery, parotidectomy) weakens it: the lower lip fails to depress on that side. Asymmetric crying facies of newborns is hypoplasia of the adjacent depressor anguli oris, linked to 22q11 deletion.

name: Mentalis
function: Elevates and protrudes the lower lip and wrinkles the skin of the chin (doubt, pouting).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Incisive fossa of the mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the chin

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Marginal mandibular branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises and protrudes the lower lip; dimples the chin

pearl: The mental nerve (V3) exits the mental foramen just lateral to it; new chin numbness ('numb chin syndrome') suggests mandibular metastasis or lymphoma until proven otherwise.

name: Platysma
function: Thin subcutaneous sheet over the anterolateral neck; tenses the skin of the neck, depresses the mandible and draws the corner of the mouth downward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid (skin of upper chest)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior border of the mandible, skin of the lower face and modiolus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Cervical branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Tenses neck skin, depresses mandible and angle of mouth (grimace of horror)

pearl: Platysma defines a penetrating neck injury: a wound that violates platysma mandates zone-based evaluation (CT angiography or exploration) and must never be probed blindly.

name: Auricular muscles (anterior, superior, posterior)
function: Three vestigial muscles that draw the auricle slightly forward, upward and backward; grouped with the epicranial (scalp) muscles and of no functional importance in humans.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior: temporal fascia. Superior: galea aponeurotica (epicranial aponeurosis). Posterior: mastoid process

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Auricular cartilage (helix, eminence of the concha)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior and superior: temporal branches of CN VII. Posterior: posterior auricular branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Draw the auricle forward, upward and backward (vestigial)

pearl: The posterior auricular nerve is the first branch of CN VII after it exits the stylomastoid foramen; its loss is clinically silent, so ear movement is not part of the facial nerve exam. Facial palsy is graded on brow, eye closure and mouth.

name: Masseter
function: Most powerful elevator of the mandible (jaw closing); its superficial fibers also protrude the jaw. Covers the lateral surface of the ramus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superficial part: anterior two-thirds of the lower border of the zygomatic arch. Deep part: medial surface of the zygomatic arch

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral surface of the ramus, angle and coronoid process of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Masseteric nerve from the anterior division of V3

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates the mandible; superficial fibers protrude

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Masseteric branch of the maxillary artery

pearl: Jaw clenching tests V3 motor function; a lower motor neuron V3 lesion causes masseter wasting. Spread of a molar infection into the masticator space causes trismus.

name: Temporalis
function: Elevates the mandible; its posterior horizontal fibers retract the protruded jaw. A fan-shaped muscle that fills the temporal fossa.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Temporal fossa (below the inferior temporal line) and deep temporal fascia

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Coronoid process and anterior border of the ramus via a tendon passing deep to the zygomatic arch

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior and posterior deep temporal nerves from the anterior division of V3

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates mandible (anterior fibers); retracts mandible (posterior fibers)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep temporal arteries (maxillary) and middle temporal artery (superficial temporal)

pearl: Jaw claudication in giant cell arteritis reflects ischemia of temporalis and masseter. The superficial temporal artery biopsied for diagnosis runs in the superficial (temporoparietal) fascia, superficial to the deep temporal fascia, where the temporal branch of CN VII is at risk.

name: Medial pterygoid
function: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; acting with the lateral pterygoid of one side it swings the jaw to the opposite side for grinding.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Deep head: medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate and pyramidal process of the palatine bone. Superficial head: maxillary tuberosity

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Medial surface of the ramus and angle of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to medial pterygoid from the main trunk of V3

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and protrudes mandible; unilateral action moves jaw to the opposite side

pearl: With masseter it forms the pterygomandibular sling around the angle; an inferior alveolar nerve block injected into the muscle causes hematoma and prolonged trismus.

name: Lateral pterygoid
function: Protrudes the mandible and pulls the condyle and articular disc forward to open the jaw; alternating sides grinds. The only masticatory muscle that opens the mouth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper head: infratemporal surface and crest of the greater wing of the sphenoid. Lower head: lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the condyle; articular disc and capsule of the TMJ

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to lateral pterygoid from the anterior division of V3 (often via the buccal nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Protrudes and depresses mandible (with suprahyoids); unilateral action deviates jaw to the opposite side

pearl: In a unilateral V3 lesion the jaw deviates toward the weak side on opening. A condyle pulled anterior to the articular eminence is an anterior TMJ dislocation, reduced with downward-backward pressure.

name: Superior rectus
function: Primary elevator of the eye, with secondary adduction and intorsion. Tested as a pure elevator with the eye abducted (looking up and out).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior part of the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) at the orbital apex

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Superior sclera about 7.7 mm posterior to the limbus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Superior division of CN III (oculomotor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevation (primary); adduction and intorsion (secondary)

pearl: CN III palsy: the eye rests 'down and out' with ptosis; a dilated pupil points to compression (posterior communicating artery aneurysm), pupil sparing to diabetic microvascular ischemia.

name: Inferior rectus
function: Primary depressor of the eye, with secondary adduction and extorsion. Tested as a pure depressor with the eye abducted (looking down and out).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior part of the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior sclera about 6.5 mm posterior to the limbus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Inferior division of CN III (oculomotor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Depression (primary); adduction and extorsion (secondary)

pearl: Entrapped in an orbital floor blowout fracture: restricted upgaze with vertical diplopia and infraorbital numbness; traction on it triggers the oculocardiac (bradycardic) reflex.

name: Medial rectus
function: Adducts the eye (its sole action); the largest and strongest extraocular muscle. Yoked with the contralateral lateral rectus during horizontal gaze.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial part of the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Medial sclera about 5.5 mm posterior to the limbus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Inferior division of CN III (oculomotor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adduction

pearl: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (MLF lesion, e.g. multiple sclerosis): the ipsilateral eye fails to adduct on lateral gaze with abducting nystagmus of the other eye, but convergence is intact.

name: Lateral rectus
function: Abducts the eye (its sole action); the only muscle supplied by the abducens nerve.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lateral part of the common tendinous ring (two heads spanning the superior orbital fissure)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral sclera about 6.9 mm posterior to the limbus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN VI (abducens)

details.label: Action
details.value: Abduction

pearl: CN VI palsy causes esotropia with horizontal diplopia worst in lateral gaze; its long intracranial course makes it a false-localizing sign of raised intracranial pressure.

name: Superior oblique
function: Primary intorsion with secondary depression and abduction; its tendon reflects through the trochlea, so it depresses the adducted eye (looking down and in).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Body of the sphenoid, superomedial to the optic canal (outside the annulus of Zinn)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Via the trochlea (fibrocartilaginous pulley on the frontal bone) to the posterolateral superior sclera behind the equator

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN IV (trochlear)

details.label: Action
details.value: Intorsion (primary); depression and abduction (secondary)

pearl: CN IV palsy: vertical diplopia worse reading or descending stairs with head tilt away from the lesion; the thin, dorsally exiting nerve is the one most often injured by head trauma.

name: Inferior oblique
function: Primary extorsion with secondary elevation and abduction; elevates the adducted eye (looking up and in). The only extraocular muscle arising from the front of the orbit.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Orbital surface of the maxilla, lateral to the nasolacrimal groove (anteromedial orbital floor)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterolateral inferior sclera behind the equator, near the macula

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Inferior division of CN III (oculomotor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Extorsion (primary); elevation and abduction (secondary)

pearl: Inferior oblique overaction is a hallmark of long-standing CN IV palsy; the muscle is at risk during blowout fracture repair and lower lid blepharoplasty, causing torsional diplopia.

name: Levator palpebrae superioris
function: Elevates the upper eyelid; a striated muscle whose aponeurosis fans into the lid skin and the anterior surface of the superior tarsal plate.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lesser wing of the sphenoid, above the optic canal and annulus of Zinn

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the upper eyelid and anterior surface of the superior tarsal plate (via the levator aponeurosis)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Superior division of CN III (oculomotor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the upper eyelid

pearl: Complete ptosis = CN III palsy; mild ptosis = Horner syndrome (superior tarsal); fatigable ptosis = myasthenia gravis; aponeurotic dehiscence = involutional ptosis of aging.

name: Superior tarsal (Müller's) muscle
function: Sympathetically driven smooth muscle that holds the upper lid about 2 mm higher; responsible for the lid widening of sympathetic arousal.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Undersurface of levator palpebrae superioris (smooth muscle slip)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Superior margin of the superior tarsal plate

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion via the internal carotid plexus and ophthalmic nerve

details.label: Action
details.value: Assists lid elevation; widens the palpebral fissure

pearl: Its loss produces the mild (1–2 mm) ptosis of Horner syndrome with miosis and anhidrosis; causes include Pancoast tumor, carotid dissection and lateral medullary stroke.

name: Stapedius
function: Smallest skeletal muscle; contracts reflexively to loud sound, stiffening the stapes and damping transmission to the cochlea (acoustic reflex).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inside the pyramidal eminence on the posterior wall of the tympanic cavity

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Neck of the stapes

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to stapedius, a branch of CN VII within the facial canal

details.label: Action
details.value: Pulls stapes posteriorly, dampening oscillation of the oval window; protects against loud noise

pearl: Hyperacusis in Bell palsy or any CN VII lesion proximal to the nerve to stapedius; an absent acoustic (stapedial) reflex on tympanometry helps localize the lesion.

name: Tensor tympani
function: Tenses the tympanic membrane by pulling the malleus medially, damping low-frequency sound such as chewing and one's own voice.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Cartilaginous part of the auditory (Eustachian) tube, greater wing of the sphenoid and the wall of its own semicanal above the tube

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Handle (manubrium) of the malleus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to medial pterygoid from V3, passing through the otic ganglion without synapsing

details.label: Action
details.value: Draws malleus medially, tensing the tympanic membrane and reducing sound transmission

pearl: Innervated by V3, not VII, so the sound sensitivity of facial palsy is from stapedius loss; tensor tympani myoclonus causes a rhythmic clicking tinnitus.

name: Digastric (anterior & posterior bellies)
function: Two-bellied suprahyoid muscle that elevates the hyoid during swallowing and depresses the mandible against resistance; its bellies define the submandibular and carotid triangles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior belly: digastric fossa of mandible. Posterior belly: mastoid notch of temporal bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Intermediate tendon tethered to body/greater horn of hyoid by a fibrous sling

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior belly: nerve to mylohyoid (CN V3). Posterior belly: digastric branch of CN VII

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates hyoid; depresses mandible when hyoid is fixed (opens mouth)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Posterior belly crosses superficial to ICA, IJV, CN X, XI, XII

pearl: Different embryologic arches explain dual innervation: anterior belly (1st arch, V3) vs posterior belly (2nd arch, VII). Posterior belly is the surgical landmark for CN XII and the carotid.

name: Mylohyoid
function: Forms the muscular floor of the mouth (oral diaphragm), elevating the hyoid, floor of mouth and tongue during swallowing and speech.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Mylohyoid line of mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Median raphe (with contralateral muscle) and body of hyoid

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to mylohyoid (branch of inferior alveolar nerve, CN V3)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates hyoid and floor of mouth; supports tongue; depresses mandible

details.label: Relations
details.value: Separates sublingual space (above) from submandibular space (below); deep part of submandibular gland hooks round its free posterior edge

pearl: Ludwig angina: bilateral cellulitis of submandibular and sublingual spaces (often from a 2nd/3rd molar whose root lies below the mylohyoid line) pushes the tongue up and back, threatening the airway.

name: Geniohyoid
function: Short paired muscle above the mylohyoid that pulls the hyoid forward and upward, widening the pharynx during swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior genial (mental) spine of mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Body of hyoid

details.label: Innervation
details.value: C1 anterior ramus fibers carried by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Draws hyoid anterosuperiorly; depresses mandible when hyoid fixed

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies superior to mylohyoid, inferior to genioglossus

pearl: Geniohyoid and thyrohyoid are supplied by C1 travelling with CN XII, not by XII itself, so an intracranial XII lesion spares them while a lesion of the nerve below C1 joining affects them.

name: Stylohyoid
function: Slender muscle from the styloid process that elevates and retracts the hyoid, lengthening the floor of the mouth during swallowing; its tendon splits around the digastric intermediate tendon.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of styloid process

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Body of hyoid at junction with greater horn (perforated by digastric tendon)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Stylohyoid branch of CN VII (facial nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and retracts hyoid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs parallel and superior to posterior belly of digastric

pearl: One of the three styloid muscles (stylohyoid VII, styloglossus XII, stylopharyngeus IX): a classic three-nerve exam point. Elongated styloid/calcified stylohyoid ligament = Eagle syndrome (throat and ear pain on swallowing).

name: Sternohyoid
function: Most superficial strap muscle; depresses the hyoid after it has been elevated in swallowing and stabilizes it for speech.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior manubrium and medial end of clavicle

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Body of hyoid

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3)

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses hyoid; fixes hyoid for suprahyoid action

details.label: Relations
details.value: Covers sternothyroid and thyrohyoid; muscles diverge inferiorly leaving a midline gap over the trachea

pearl: Strap muscles overlie the thyroid; in thyroidectomy they are retracted laterally or, if division is needed, cut in their upper half because ansa cervicalis branches enter inferiorly, preserving innervation of most of the muscle.

name: Omohyoid
function: Two-bellied strap muscle whose intermediate tendon is tethered to the clavicle; depresses and retracts the hyoid and subdivides both anterior and posterior triangles of the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior belly: superior border of scapula near suprascapular notch

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Superior belly: body of hyoid; intermediate tendon bound to clavicle by a fascial sling

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3)

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses, retracts and steadies hyoid; tenses deep cervical fascia (helps keep IJV patent)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior belly divides anterior triangle into carotid and muscular triangles; inferior belly divides posterior triangle into occipital and supraclavicular (subclavian) triangles

pearl: Classic intraoperative landmark for the level III/IV junction (current AAO-HNS/AJCC levels use the inferior border of the cricoid instead); inferior belly lies just above the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus.

name: Sternothyroid
function: Strap muscle deep to sternohyoid that depresses the larynx (thyroid cartilage) and prevents upward spread of the thyroid gland.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior manubrium and 1st costal cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage lamina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Ansa cervicalis (C2–C3)

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses larynx and thyroid cartilage after swallowing/phonation

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies directly on thyroid gland and inferior thyroid vein

pearl: Because sternothyroid attaches to the oblique line, a goitre cannot enlarge upward past the thyroid cartilage and instead extends inferiorly (retrosternal goitre, Pemberton sign).

name: Thyrohyoid
function: Short strap muscle continuing the line of sternothyroid; depresses the hyoid or, when the hyoid is fixed, elevates the larynx during swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior border of body and greater horn of hyoid

details.label: Innervation
details.value: C1 anterior ramus fibers via the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII), not the ansa

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses hyoid; elevates larynx when hyoid fixed

details.label: Relations
details.value: Internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal artery pierce thyrohyoid membrane just posterior to it

pearl: Exception among infrahyoids: supplied by C1 via XII rather than ansa cervicalis. The thyrohyoid membrane behind it is where the internal laryngeal nerve enters (site of superior laryngeal nerve block).

name: Sternocleidomastoid
function: Key landmark dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles; unilaterally tilts the head ipsilaterally and rotates the face contralaterally; bilaterally flexes the neck and aids forced inspiration.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Sternal head: anterior manubrium. Clavicular head: medial third of clavicle

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral surface of mastoid process and lateral half of superior nuchal line

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) motor; C2–C3 anterior rami proprioception

details.label: Action
details.value: Unilateral: tilts head to same side, rotates face to opposite side. Bilateral: flexes neck, extends head, accessory inspiratory muscle

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, superior thyroid and posterior auricular arteries

pearl: Congenital torticollis: fibrosis/shortening of one SCM tilts the head toward the lesion and rotates the chin away. CN XI emerges from the posterior border at the junction of its upper and middle thirds and is at risk in posterior-triangle lymph node biopsy.

name: Trapezius
function: Large superficial muscle forming the posterior border of the posterior triangle; its upper fibers elevate the scapula and shrug the shoulder, and it rotates the scapula upward for arm abduction above 90 degrees.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior nuchal line, external occipital protuberance, ligamentum nuchae, spinous processes C7–T12

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral third of clavicle, acromion, spine of scapula

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) motor; C3–C4 anterior rami proprioception

details.label: Action
details.value: Upper: elevates scapula; middle: retracts; lower: depresses; upper + lower rotate glenoid upward

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Transverse cervical artery (superficial branch)

pearl: CN XI injury in the posterior triangle (lymph node biopsy, neck dissection) causes shoulder droop, weak shrug, impaired abduction above the shoulder and lateral scapular winging; SCM is spared if the injury is distal.

name: Anterior scalene
function: Key relational muscle of the root of the neck: the subclavian vein passes anterior to it and the subclavian artery and brachial plexus posterior; elevates the first rib and laterally flexes the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior tubercles of transverse processes C3–C6

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Scalene tubercle of 1st rib

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C4–C6

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates 1st rib (inspiration); flexes and laterally flexes neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Phrenic nerve descends on its anterior surface; subclavian vein anterior, subclavian artery and brachial plexus trunks posterior

pearl: The phrenic nerve lies on the anterior scalene under prevertebral fascia, so the interscalene brachial plexus block almost always causes transient ipsilateral hemidiaphragm paralysis.

name: Middle scalene
function: Largest scalene; with the anterior scalene it bounds the interscalene triangle through which the subclavian artery and brachial plexus trunks pass to the axilla.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes C2–C7

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper surface of 1st rib posterior to groove for subclavian artery

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C3–C8

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates 1st rib; laterally flexes neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pierced by the dorsal scapular nerve (C5) and the C5 and C6 roots of the long thoracic nerve; the C7 root passes anterior to the muscle

pearl: Thoracic outlet syndrome: compression of the brachial plexus (usually lower trunk, C8–T1) or subclavian artery between anterior and middle scalenes, worsened by a cervical rib; ulnar-sided paresthesias, arm claudication.

name: Posterior scalene
function: Smallest and most posterior scalene; elevates the second rib in inspiration and laterally flexes the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes C5–C7

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Outer surface of 2nd rib

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C6–C8

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates 2nd rib; laterally flexes neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Forms part of the floor of the posterior triangle with middle scalene, levator scapulae and splenius capitis

pearl: Scalenes are accessory muscles of inspiration; visible scalene and SCM contraction at rest indicates severe respiratory distress (e.g. COPD exacerbation, status asthmaticus).

name: Splenius capitis
function: Broad strap-like extensor in the floor of the posterior triangle that extends, laterally flexes and rotates the head to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lower ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes C7–T3

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Mastoid process and lateral third of superior nuchal line (deep to SCM)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Lateral branches of posterior rami of middle cervical nerves (C3–C4)

details.label: Action
details.value: Unilateral: ipsilateral rotation and lateral flexion of head. Bilateral: extension

details.label: Relations
details.value: Forms floor of upper posterior triangle; covered by trapezius and SCM

pearl: Splenius rotates the head to the SAME side, whereas SCM rotates it to the OPPOSITE side, so ipsilateral splenius and contralateral SCM act together in head rotation.

name: Levator scapulae
function: Strap muscle in the floor of the posterior triangle that elevates the scapula and rotates its glenoid downward; laterally flexes the neck when the scapula is fixed.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes C1–C4

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Medial border of scapula from superior angle to root of spine

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C3–C4 and dorsal scapular nerve (C5)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates scapula; rotates glenoid inferiorly; lateral neck flexion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Spinal accessory nerve crosses its surface in the posterior triangle

pearl: CN XI runs superficial to levator scapulae in the posterior triangle; levator scapulae and rhomboids partially compensate for shoulder elevation after accessory nerve injury but cannot prevent the droop.

name: Longus colli
function: Longest prevertebral muscle, lying on the anterior surfaces of the vertebral bodies from the atlas to T3 behind the retropharyngeal space; flexes and slightly rotates the cervical spine.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Three parts: vertical (bodies C5–T3), inferior oblique (bodies T1–T3), superior oblique (anterior tubercles of transverse processes C3–C5)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Vertical: bodies C2–C4. Inferior oblique: anterior tubercles of transverse processes C5–C6. Superior oblique: anterior tubercle of atlas

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C2–C6

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes neck; lateral flexion; inferior oblique part rotates to the opposite side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Covered by prevertebral fascia, which forms the posterior wall of the retropharyngeal space; cervical sympathetic trunk lies on it, posterior to the carotid sheath

pearl: Acute calcific tendinitis of longus colli (hydroxyapatite in the superior oblique fibers at C1–C2) mimics retropharyngeal abscess: acute neck pain, odynophagia, prevertebral swelling. CT shows amorphous calcification anterior to C1–C2 with prevertebral fluid but no rim-enhancing collection; treat with NSAIDs, not drainage.

name: Longus capitis
function: Prevertebral muscle from the cervical transverse processes to the skull base that flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior tubercles of transverse processes C3–C6

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Basilar part of occipital bone anterior to foramen magnum

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami C1–C3

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes head on neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterolateral to the upper part of longus colli; posterior to the pharynx and posteromedial to the carotid sheath; cervical sympathetic trunk lies on its anterior surface

pearl: Whiplash strains the prevertebral flexors (longus capitis/colli); prevertebral soft-tissue widening on lateral C-spine X-ray (>7 mm at C2, >21 mm at C7) suggests occult fracture, ligamentous injury or hematoma and warrants CT.

name: Rectus capitis anterior & lateralis
function: Two small muscles between the atlas and the occipital bone that flex (anterior) and laterally flex (lateralis) the head at the atlanto-occipital joint and stabilize it.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior: anterior surface of lateral mass of atlas. Lateralis: transverse process of atlas

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Anterior: basilar occiput anterior to condyle. Lateralis: jugular process of occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami of C1 and C2

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexion and lateral flexion of the head; postural stabilization

details.label: Relations
details.value: Rectus capitis lateralis lies just posterior to the internal jugular vein exiting the jugular foramen

pearl: Rectus capitis lateralis is the landmark separating the IJV (anterior) from the vertebral artery (posterior) at the skull base; it is a surgical guide in approaches to the jugular foramen.

name: Suboccipital muscles (suboccipital triangle)
function: Four small muscles (rectus capitis posterior major/minor, obliquus capitis superior/inferior) that extend and rotate the head at the atlanto-occipital and atlanto-axial joints; three bound the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of axis (RCP major, obliquus inferior); posterior tubercle of atlas (RCP minor); transverse process of atlas (obliquus superior)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior nuchal line of occiput (RCP major lateral, RCP minor medial); occiput between superior and inferior nuchal lines (obliquus superior); transverse process of atlas (obliquus inferior)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Action
details.value: Extension and ipsilateral rotation of head; fine postural control

details.label: Triangle contents
details.value: Vertebral artery (3rd part) in groove on posterior arch of atlas, suboccipital nerve (C1), suboccipital venous plexus

pearl: Vertebral artery loops through the suboccipital triangle before piercing the dura; vertebral artery dissection here (chiropractic manipulation, trauma) causes occipital headache and lateral medullary (Wallenberg) signs.

name: Semispinalis capitis
function: Thick extensor of the head forming the longitudinal bulge on each side of the posterior neck deep to trapezius; extends the head and neck and is pierced by the greater occipital nerve.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse processes C7–T6 and articular processes C4–C6

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Occipital bone between superior and inferior nuchal lines

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves (incl. C2 greater occipital nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends head and cervical spine; slight contralateral rotation

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to trapezius and splenius; roof of suboccipital triangle; pierced by greater occipital nerve (C2)

pearl: Occipital neuralgia: greater occipital nerve entrapment where it pierces semispinalis capitis and trapezius causes shooting occiput-to-vertex pain; block at the superior nuchal line, medial to the occipital artery.

name: Longissimus capitis
function: Cephalic continuation of the erector spinae that extends the head and rotates it to the same side; lies between splenius and semispinalis capitis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse processes T1–T5 and articular processes C4–C7

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior margin of mastoid process (deep to splenius capitis and SCM)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends head; ipsilateral lateral flexion and rotation

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral to semispinalis capitis, deep to splenius capitis

pearl: Paraspinal (longissimus/erector spinae) spasm is the usual source of mechanical neck pain after whiplash; imaging after blunt trauma is driven by midline bony tenderness, neurological deficit, intoxication, altered mentation or dangerous mechanism (NEXUS criteria / Canadian C-spine rule), not by paraspinal tenderness.

name: Splenius cervicis
function: Lower, narrower part of the splenius sheet; extends, laterally flexes and ipsilaterally rotates the cervical spine.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous processes T3–T6

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes C1–C3

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of lower cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Action
details.value: Unilateral: ipsilateral rotation and lateral flexion of neck. Bilateral: extension

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to trapezius and rhomboids; covers semispinalis cervicis and erector spinae

pearl: Cervical dystonia (spasmodic torticollis) frequently involves splenius and SCM; botulinum toxin injected into splenius cervicis/capitis treats laterocollis and rotation toward the injected side.

name: Semispinalis cervicis
function: Deep transversospinalis muscle beneath semispinalis capitis that extends and contralaterally rotates the cervical spine; attaches heavily to the spinous process of the axis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse processes T1–T6

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous processes C2–C5 (thickest bundle to axis)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Medial branches of posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends cervical spine; contralateral rotation

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to semispinalis capitis; superficial to multifidus

pearl: Spinous process of C2 is the anchor for semispinalis cervicis and the suboccipital rotators; its large bifid tip is palpable just below the occiput as the first midline bony landmark.

name: Superior pharyngeal constrictor
function: Uppermost constrictor forming the wall of the nasopharynx and oropharynx; contracts sequentially with the other constrictors to propel the bolus and helps close the nasopharynx (Passavant ridge) with the soft palate.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe, posterior mylohyoid line of mandible, side of tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Pharyngeal tubercle of basiocciput and median pharyngeal raphe

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (motor fibers of CN X with cranial root of XI)

details.label: Action
details.value: Constricts upper pharynx; forms Passavant ridge during velopharyngeal closure

details.label: Gaps
details.value: Above its upper border (sinus of Morgagni): auditory tube and levator veli palatini. Between superior and middle: stylopharyngeus and CN IX

pearl: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (EBV-associated) arises in the fossa of Rosenmuller above the superior constrictor; presents with unilateral serous otitis media, epistaxis and level II/V neck nodes.

name: Middle pharyngeal constrictor
function: Fan-shaped constrictor arising from the hyoid that overlaps the superior constrictor and squeezes the bolus through the oropharynx toward the laryngopharynx.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Greater and lesser horns of hyoid and stylohyoid ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Median pharyngeal raphe (overlapping superior constrictor externally)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X motor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Constricts mid-pharynx during deglutition

details.label: Gaps
details.value: Between middle and inferior constrictor: internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal artery (through thyrohyoid membrane)

pearl: Each constrictor overlaps the one above from outside, so a bolus is pushed down; gaps between them transmit nerves and vessels, and are routes for pharyngeal abscess or tumor spread into the parapharyngeal space.

name: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor (incl. cricopharyngeus)
function: Thickest constrictor with thyropharyngeus (oblique) and cricopharyngeus (horizontal, the upper esophageal sphincter) parts; propels the bolus into the esophagus and keeps the UES closed between swallows.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage (thyropharyngeus) and side of cricoid cartilage (cricopharyngeus)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Median pharyngeal raphe; cricopharyngeus continuous with circular esophageal muscle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X), plus external laryngeal and recurrent laryngeal nerve branches to cricopharyngeus

details.label: Action
details.value: Constricts laryngopharynx; cricopharyngeus is tonically contracted as the UES, relaxing during swallowing

details.label: Gaps
details.value: Below inferior border: recurrent laryngeal nerve and inferior laryngeal artery. Killian's dehiscence between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus

pearl: Zenker diverticulum: false (pulsion) diverticulum through Killian's dehiscence from cricopharyngeal spasm; elderly dysphagia, halitosis, regurgitated undigested food; barium swallow to diagnose, avoid blind NG tube.

name: Stylopharyngeus
function: Longitudinal pharyngeal muscle from the styloid process that elevates and widens the pharynx and larynx during swallowing; the only muscle innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial side of base of styloid process

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior border of thyroid cartilage lamina and pharyngeal wall, passing between superior and middle constrictors

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN IX (glossopharyngeal nerve), motor branch

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates pharynx and larynx; widens pharynx to receive bolus

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN IX winds around its posterolateral border; passes between ICA and ECA

pearl: Stylopharyngeus is the sole motor target of CN IX; CN IX lesion is tested by the gag reflex (IX afferent, X efferent) and loss of taste/sensation on the posterior third of the tongue.

name: Palatopharyngeus
function: Longitudinal muscle forming the posterior tonsillar pillar (palatopharyngeal arch); elevates the pharynx and larynx and pulls the palatopharyngeal arches medially to seal the oropharyngeal isthmus during swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Palatine aponeurosis and posterior border of hard palate

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior border of thyroid cartilage lamina and lateral pharyngeal wall

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X motor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates pharynx and larynx; depresses soft palate toward tongue; approximates palatopharyngeal arches to close oropharyngeal isthmus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Posterior boundary of tonsillar fossa; palatine tonsil lies between it and palatoglossus

pearl: Palatopharyngeal arch is the posterior tonsillar pillar; peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) bulges the soft palate and pillar, displacing the uvula to the contralateral side with trismus and a hot-potato voice.

name: Salpingopharyngeus
function: Thin longitudinal muscle from the auditory tube cartilage that raises the salpingopharyngeal fold; elevates the pharynx and helps open the auditory tube during swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior aspect of cartilaginous auditory (Eustachian) tube near torus tubarius

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Blends with palatopharyngeus in lateral pharyngeal wall

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X motor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates pharynx; assists opening of auditory tube

details.label: Relations
details.value: Forms salpingopharyngeal fold descending from torus tubarius in nasopharynx

pearl: Eustachian tube dysfunction in children relates to a shorter, more horizontal tube; the fossa of Rosenmuller lies behind the torus tubarius and is the classic site of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

name: Genioglossus
function: Fan-shaped extrinsic tongue muscle and the bulk of the tongue; protrudes the tongue and depresses its center, keeping the airway open by pulling the tongue base forward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior genial (mental) spine of mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Entire length of dorsum of tongue and body of hyoid

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN XII (hypoglossal nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Protrudes tongue; depresses central tongue; posterior fibers pull tongue base forward (airway patency)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingual artery and CN XII lateral to it; hypoglossal nerve lies lateral to hyoglossus

pearl: CN XII LMN lesion: tongue deviates TOWARD the weak side on protrusion (unopposed contralateral genioglossus) with ipsilateral atrophy and fasciculations. Loss of genioglossus tone in sleep contributes to OSA.

name: Hyoglossus
function: Thin quadrilateral extrinsic muscle from the hyoid that depresses and retracts the tongue; a key landmark separating the lingual artery (deep) from the hypoglossal nerve and lingual vein (superficial).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Body and greater horn of hyoid

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Side and inferior surface of tongue, interdigitating with styloglossus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN XII (hypoglossal nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Depresses and retracts tongue; flattens tongue sides

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superficial (lateral): CN XII, lingual nerve, submandibular duct. Deep (medial): lingual artery, CN IX, stylohyoid ligament

pearl: Lingual artery ligation for tongue hemorrhage is done deep to hyoglossus (Lesser triangle, bounded by the digastric bellies and CN XII); CN XII crosses hyoglossus superficially and must be preserved.

name: Styloglossus
function: Extrinsic tongue muscle from the styloid process that retracts and elevates the tongue, forming a trough for swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral aspect of styloid process and stylomandibular ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Side of tongue, blending with hyoglossus and intrinsic muscles

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN XII (hypoglossal nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Retracts and elevates tongue; draws sides up to create central trough

details.label: Relations
details.value: Descends between ICA and ECA, then runs forward lateral (external) to the superior constrictor and hyoglossus to enter the side of the tongue

pearl: Three styloid muscles have three different nerves: styloglossus XII, stylohyoid VII, stylopharyngeus IX. Posterior-third tongue carcinoma invades styloglossus/hyoglossus early and drains to level II nodes.

name: Palatoglossus
function: Muscle of the anterior tonsillar pillar (palatoglossal arch) that elevates the posterior tongue and pulls the palate down to close the oropharyngeal isthmus; the only tongue muscle not supplied by CN XII.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Palatine aponeurosis of soft palate

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Side of tongue, blending with transverse intrinsic fibers

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X), via cranial root of CN XI

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates posterior tongue; depresses soft palate; narrows oropharyngeal isthmus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior boundary of tonsillar fossa; palatine tonsil between it and palatopharyngeus

pearl: A palate muscle by innervation (CN X), so hypoglossal palsy spares it. The palatoglossal arch marks the oropharyngeal boundary; the tonsillar branch of the facial artery behind it bleeds after tonsillectomy.

name: Intrinsic tongue muscles
function: Four paired muscles entirely within the tongue (superior and inferior longitudinal, transverse, vertical) that alter its shape for speech, chewing and swallowing without moving its position.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Within the tongue: median fibrous septum and lingual aponeurosis

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Within the tongue substance (no bony attachment)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: CN XII (hypoglossal nerve)

details.label: Action
details.value: Superior longitudinal curls tip up/shortens; inferior longitudinal curls tip down; transverse narrows and elongates; vertical flattens and widens

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual artery (branch of lingual artery)

pearl: Bulbar (LMN) palsy such as ALS causes tongue atrophy and fasciculations from intrinsic and extrinsic muscle denervation, whereas pseudobulbar (UMN) palsy gives a spastic, slow tongue without wasting.

name: Levator veli palatini
function: Principal elevator of the soft palate that closes the nasopharynx during swallowing and speech (velopharyngeal closure) and assists opening of the auditory tube.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Petrous temporal bone anterior to carotid canal and cartilage of auditory tube

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper surface of palatine aponeurosis, passing above the superior constrictor

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X motor via cranial root of XI)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and retracts soft palate against posterior pharyngeal wall

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies inferomedial to auditory tube; forms a bulge below the torus tubarius

pearl: Vagal (CN X) lesion: uvula deviates AWAY from the lesion side on saying 'ah' because the intact levator pulls the palate up; nasal regurgitation and hypernasal speech follow velopharyngeal insufficiency.

name: Tensor veli palatini
function: Tenses the soft palate and is the main muscle that opens the auditory tube to equalize middle-ear pressure; its tendon hooks round the pterygoid hamulus, forming the palatine aponeurosis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Scaphoid fossa of medial pterygoid plate, spine of sphenoid, lateral membranous wall of auditory tube

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Tendon turns 90 degrees around pterygoid hamulus to form palatine aponeurosis

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to medial pterygoid (CN V3), the only palate muscle not supplied by X

details.label: Action
details.value: Tenses soft palate; opens auditory tube (with levator)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies lateral to levator veli palatini and medial pterygoid plate

pearl: Tensor veli palatini is the V3 exception among palate muscles (tensors tympani and veli palatini = V3). Tensor dysfunction underlies chronic otitis media with effusion in cleft palate; repair re-orients the levator.

name: Musculus uvulae
function: Small midline muscle within the uvula that shortens and elevates it, thickening the central soft palate to help complete velopharyngeal closure.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior nasal spine of palatine bone and palatine aponeurosis

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Mucosa of uvula

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pharyngeal plexus (CN X motor)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens and elevates uvula; adds bulk to the dorsum of the soft palate for nasopharyngeal seal

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the two layers of palatine aponeurosis in the midline

pearl: A bifid uvula may be the only visible sign of submucous cleft palate (absent musculus uvulae in the midline); avoid adenoidectomy in these children as it can unmask velopharyngeal insufficiency.

name: Cricothyroid
function: Only intrinsic laryngeal muscle on the external surface of the larynx; tilts the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid to lengthen and tense the vocal folds, raising pitch.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral arch of cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior horn and lower border of thyroid cartilage lamina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve (CN X) - the only intrinsic muscle not supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve

details.label: Action
details.value: Tenses and lengthens vocal folds (increases pitch)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior thyroid artery runs with the external laryngeal nerve near its upper pole attachment

pearl: External laryngeal nerve injury (superior thyroid artery ligation at thyroidectomy) paralyzes cricothyroid: lost high pitch and vocal fatigue, normal-looking cord on laryngoscopy. Cricothyrotomy is via its membrane.

name: Posterior cricoarytenoid
function: The only abductor of the vocal folds; rotates the arytenoids laterally to open the rima glottidis for breathing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of cricoid lamina

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Action
details.value: Abducts vocal folds (laterally rotates arytenoids); opens rima glottidis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies on back of cricoid beneath the laryngopharyngeal mucosa

pearl: Bilateral RLN injury (thyroidectomy) paralyzes both PCAs (sole abductors); cords lie paramedian, classically attributed to the intact cricothyroid (SLN), causing stridor and obstruction needing emergency tracheostomy.

name: Lateral cricoarytenoid
function: Main adductor of the vocal folds; rotates the arytenoids medially to close the rima glottidis for phonation and airway protection.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper border of arch of cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts vocal folds (medially rotates arytenoids); closes membranous glottis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies deep to thyroid lamina, lateral to the conus elasticus

pearl: Unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy: hoarse, breathy voice with a bowed paramedian cord and ineffective cough; evaluate for lung apex tumor, aortic arch aneurysm (left) or post-thyroidectomy injury.

name: Thyroarytenoid (incl. vocalis)
function: Muscle forming the body of the vocal fold; relaxes and shortens the fold to lower pitch, with its medial vocalis portion fine-tuning tension of segments of the fold.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of thyroid cartilage angle

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Anterolateral surface and vocal process of arytenoid; vocalis fibers insert along vocal ligament

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens and relaxes vocal folds (lowers pitch); adducts; vocalis adjusts tension locally

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral to vocal ligament; upper fibers extend to epiglottis as thyroepiglottic part

pearl: True vocal fold: stratified squamous epithelium over vocalis; smoking and alcohol cause laryngeal SCC, presenting early with hoarseness. Hoarseness >2–4 wk (sooner in smokers or with red flags) needs laryngoscopy.

name: Transverse & oblique arytenoids
function: Interarytenoid muscles that approximate the arytenoid cartilages to close the posterior (intercartilaginous) part of the rima glottidis and, via the aryepiglottic extension, narrow the laryngeal inlet.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface and muscular process of one arytenoid

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Opposite arytenoid (transverse: unpaired, spans both; oblique: cross to apex of opposite arytenoid)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X), bilateral supply to the unpaired transverse arytenoid

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts arytenoids, closing posterior glottis; oblique part continues as aryepiglottic muscle to close inlet

details.label: Relations
details.value: Covered posteriorly by laryngopharyngeal mucosa

pearl: Both RLNs supply the unpaired transverse arytenoid, so unilateral RLN palsy still allows partial posterior glottic closure. Paramedian cord: breathy voice, weak cough, possible aspiration; bilateral palsy: stridor.

name: Aryepiglottic muscle
function: Continuation of the oblique arytenoid into the aryepiglottic fold; acts as a sphincter of the laryngeal inlet, drawing the folds together and the epiglottis backward to seal the vestibule during swallowing.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Apex of arytenoid cartilage (continuation of oblique arytenoid fibers)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral margin of epiglottis, running within the aryepiglottic fold

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Action
details.value: Closes the laryngeal inlet (vestibule) during deglutition; airway protection

details.label: Relations
details.value: Aryepiglottic fold contains the cuneiform cartilage and ends at the corniculate cartilage; piriform recess lies lateral to it (foreign bodies lodge here; internal laryngeal nerve runs beneath its mucosa)

pearl: Supraglottic cancer and epiglottitis both involve the aryepiglottic folds. Adult with sore throat, muffled 'hot potato' voice, drooling and stridor: thumb-sign epiglottis with thickened aryepiglottic folds on lateral neck X-ray means impending airway loss; secure the airway first. Supraglottic tumors metastasize to nodes early (rich lymphatics), unlike glottic tumors.

name: Thyroepiglottic muscle
function: Upper slip of the thyroarytenoid that runs to the epiglottis and widens the laryngeal inlet, opposing the aryepiglottic sphincter action.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inner surface of thyroid cartilage lamina (superior fibers of thyroarytenoid)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral margin of epiglottis and aryepiglottic fold

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Action
details.value: Widens the laryngeal inlet by acting on the aryepiglottic folds (Gray's/Snell: the inlet's dilator, antagonist of the aryepiglottic/oblique arytenoid sphincter). Its effect on the epiglottis itself is contested: a minority of sources describe slight epiglottic lowering or inlet closure during swallowing, so do not learn it as an epiglottic depressor.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the quadrangular membrane region lateral to the laryngeal vestibule

pearl: All intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid are RLN territory; the left RLN loops under the aortic arch, so left vocal cord palsy can herald lung cancer or an enlarged left atrium (Ortner syndrome).

name: Sphincter pupillae
function: Circular smooth muscle of the iris; parasympathetic contraction constricts the pupil (miosis) in the light and near reflexes, limiting light entry and improving depth of focus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Circular smooth-muscle fibers (neuroectoderm-derived, from the optic cup; not neural crest) within the iris stroma near the pupillary margin

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Encircles the pupillary margin as a continuous ring

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Parasympathetic: Edinger-Westphal nucleus -> CN III -> ciliary ganglion -> short ciliary nerves (M3 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Miosis; efferent limb of the pupillary light reflex and the near (accommodation) triad

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Major arterial circle of the iris (long posterior and anterior ciliary arteries)

pearl: Compressive CN III palsy (PCOM aneurysm, uncal herniation) hits superficial parasympathetic fibers first: fixed dilated pupil. Pilocarpine constricts it; tropicamide/atropine block it.

name: Dilator pupillae
function: Radial smooth muscle of the iris; sympathetic contraction widens the pupil (mydriasis) in dim light and with arousal, increasing light entry to the retina.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Radial myoepithelial fibers arising from the iris root at the ciliary margin

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Runs toward the pupillary margin, posterior/deep to the sphincter pupillae

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Sympathetic: hypothalamus -> T1 -> superior cervical ganglion -> carotid plexus -> long ciliary nerves (alpha-1 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Mydriasis; dilated pupil of the fight-or-flight response and dim-light vision

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Major arterial circle of the iris

pearl: Horner syndrome: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis. Cocaine fails to dilate; hydroxyamphetamine dilates only if lesion is pre-ganglionic; apraclonidine reverses anisocoria (denervation supersensitivity).

name: Ciliary muscle
function: Smooth muscle ring in the ciliary body; parasympathetic contraction relaxes zonular fibers so the lens rounds up for near vision, and opens the trabecular meshwork to aid aqueous outflow.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Scleral spur (anterior sclera at the corneoscleral junction)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Ciliary body stroma and choroid; longitudinal (Brucke), radial and circular (Muller) fiber groups

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Parasympathetic: CN III (Edinger-Westphal) via ciliary ganglion and short ciliary nerves (M3 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Accommodation for near vision; longitudinal fibers pull on the scleral spur, opening the trabecular meshwork to increase aqueous outflow

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior and long posterior ciliary arteries (major arterial circle)

pearl: Pilocarpine contracts it to open the trabecular meshwork (open-angle glaucoma); in acute angle closure it works mainly via miosis pulling the iris off the angle. Cycloplegics (atropine, cyclopentolate) paralyze it: blurred near vision. Presbyopia is lens stiffening, not muscle weakness; CN III palsy adds loss of accommodation.
